title: Two classes of volcanic plumes on Io
notes: Issue 2. Metadata from Semantic Scholar and USGS Pubs Warehouse.
quantitative: Abstract (USGS): Prometheus-type small plumes 'erupt at velocities of ~0.5 km sec-1', bright whitish deposits, equatorial belt, eruption duration 'at least several years'. Pele-type large plumes 'erupt at ~1.0 km sec-1', darker red deposits, restricted to 240-360 W, duration 'of the order of days to weeks'. Plume HEIGHTS (~100 / ~300 km) are NOT in the abstract: unconfirmed from this source.

title: Volcanic eruptions and climate
quantitative: Sulfate aerosol 'e-folding residence time of about 1 year'. Large explosive eruptions 'certainly produce global or hemispheric cooling for 2 or 3 years'. Superposed composite of six eruptions: cooling ~0.1-0.2 C with 'the maximum cooling is found approximately 1 year following the eruptions'. Winter warming: 'The winter following a large tropical eruption is warmer over the NH continents'. A Pinatubo-specific ~0.5 K figure was NOT found in the fetched text: unconfirmed.
